Chapter 10: Repairing After Hurt and Rebuilding Trust.
No relationship is totally immune to hurt, right? Whether it’s a misunderstanding, a broken promise, or even something bigger—trust can get shaken up. And honestly, repairing that trust isn’t just important, it’s delicate, too.
So, where do you start? It all begins with acknowledgment. That means really seeing the hurt for what it is—not brushing it off, and definitely not trying to justify it. Sometimes, it’s as simple as saying, “I see that my words hurt you, and I’m truly sorry.” A genuine apology like that, without any defensiveness, can open the door to healing.
Now, rebuilding trust? That’s a process. And it doesn’t happen overnight. It takes consistent, trustworthy actions over time. You’ve got to be open to feedback, ready to make things right, and—maybe most importantly—patient with how long healing takes. Because trust can’t be rushed.
And what about forgiveness? Well, it’s not about forgetting what happened, or pretending it was okay. Forgiveness is a choice to move forward without holding onto resentment. In a way, you’re giving that gift to yourself, as much as to the relationship.
Let’s bring this to life with a real example. Imagine after a heated argument, one partner owns up to using harsh words, offers a heartfelt apology, and really tries to communicate more gently from then on. The other partner, even though they’re still hurting, can see that effort—and, little by little, starts to feel safe reconnecting.
Remember, repair isn’t just a one-time fix. It’s an ongoing practice. Every honest conversation, every small act of care, every time you follow through on a promise—you’re laying down another brick in the foundation of trust.
